chunks: Capacitor self-resonant frequency. The question: What is a capacitor's self resonant frequency?
Every real capacitor has a little inductance in series with it, called the ESL. A capacitor's reactance falls as frequency rises, while an inductor's reactance rises.
So at some frequency they cancel. That is the self-resonant frequency (SRF), f equals 1 over (2 pi square root of L eslC ) . Below it, the part acts as a capacitor.
Above it, it acts as an inductor.
Picture a seesaw. One side is the capacitor's reactance, which is negative and shrinks in size as frequency rises.
The other side is the inductor's reactance, which is positive and growing. At the SRF, the two sides balance exactly. Before that point, the capacitor side is heavier.
After it, the inductor side wins. At the balance point, only a small resistance (the ESR) is left to oppose current.
SRF falls as 1 over square root of C and as 1 over square root of L . Quadrupling either halves the SRF. This is why the same 100 nanofarads part resonates at 22 megahertz with 0.
5 nanohenries, 16 megahertz with 1 nanohenries, and 11 megahertz with 2 nanohenries.
ESL: the small inductance of the capacitor's internal loop, leads and mounting. ESR: the small resistance in series with the capacitor.
Reactance: the frequency-dependent opposition of a capacitor or inductor. Self-resonant frequency (SRF): the frequency where capacitive and inductive reactances cancel.
Decade: a tenfold range of frequency.
A 100 nanofarads ceramic with about 1 nanohenries of total inductance has an SRF of 1 over (2 pi square root of 10 to the -9 times 10 to the -7 ) , about 16 megahertz.
A 1 microfarads part with the same 1 nanohenries has an SRF of about 5 megahertz. The bigger capacitor resonates lower. That is why designers use several values in parallel.
"The self-resonant frequency is where the capacitor's capacitive reactance cancels its own ESL's inductive reactance: f equals one over two pi root of L times C.
Below it the part is a capacitor, at it the impedance is just the ESR, above it the part is an inductor. A 100 nanofarads ceramic with 1 nanohenries is around 16 megahertz.
Bigger capacitance and more mounting inductance both lower the SRF, which is why we parallel several values and keep loops short."
